title: Adaptive Attention Contracts and KV Cache Slot Scaling for Sparse MQA quirks in Llama/Mistral/Qwen
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: In practice we observe pathological latency/throughput regressions for mixed-quality-attention (MQA/GQA) model variants when a single universal kernel choice and naive KV caching are applied. This PR introduces two complementary runtime mechanisms: (1) attention contracts, a lightweight per-request contract that encodes sparsity/stride hints and preferred kernel families (dense-fused, sparse-fused, fallback attention), and (2) KV cache slot scaling, a dynamic slot allocation and soft-eviction policy that reduces memory amplification for MQA shards while preserving prefix reuse. Design: attention contracts are produced by model introspection + sequence-length heuristics at the front of request processing and carried as a 1-byte mask + 1-byte profile id; the kernel selector consults the contract before performing cost-model scoring, biasing toward a sparse-fused kernel for MQA-style layout when sequence_length <= 1024 and head_count matches known Qwen/Mistral patterns. KV slot scaler monitors per-request unique-prefix ratio over a 1k-sample sliding window and adjusts per-shard slot_multiplier (0.5x..2.0x) with hysteresis to avoid thrash. We also add a compact slot-allocator that groups small prefixes to adjacent slots to improve locality. Implementation: changes to runtime/kernel_selector.cpp implement the contract pesos and backoff; new runtime/kv_cache/slot_scaler.rs contains the scaler state machine and eviction hooks; lightweight ABI changes add contract header propagation in runtime/transport.h; unit tests and a microbench harness were added under tests/microbench; docs and rollout notes added to docs/perf. Backwards compatibility: contracts are opt-in behind runtime flag "enable_attn_contracts" and fall back to legacy selector when not present. KV slot scaler also defaults to disabled; a controlled canary rollout is documented. Benchmarks: on internal MQA Llama-70B microbench with synthetic chat load (p95 tokens_per_second, seq len 128..512) we measured median throughput uplift of 18% and p95 latency reduction of 12-16% when both mechanisms are enabled, with memory savings of ~22% for KV allocations on mixed-prefix workloads. On Qwen-R50 tests we saw 8-10% throughput gains at mid/long sequences due to reduced kernel mis-selection. Tests and CI: full unit test coverage added for selector heuristics, scaler transitions, and eviction invariants; microbench harness runs on GPU CI tier with deterministic seeds. Rollout: gated by feature flags, stepwise canary to 10%/50%/100% of traffic with runtime metrics monitored (token latency by model, p95, kv_alloc_bytes, kernel-selection-distribution). If regression threshold exceeded (>5% p95 regression) feature flag auto-rolls back. Risks and mitigations: wrong contract bias can increase compute cost for some models; mitigated by conservative default weights and a fallback to cost-model scoring. Edge cases: models with mixed head sizes (custom Llama forks) will bypass contract bias and still use cost model. Related: references ENG-1987 (MQA regression incident), ENG-2040 (kernel selector refactor). Request: review kernel correctness on MQA head splitting and KV eviction invariants, sanity-check perf numbers and rollout gating. This is intended as an incremental, opt-in improvement to reduce operator tuning burden for MQA/GQA workloads.

review_comments: Lorenzo Diaz: Please add a short comment on the cost-model weight math in kernel_selector.cpp so future readers understand the fallback behavior. Request change.
Author (Maya Patel): Added inline math comment and a unit test demonstrating fallback path.

Author: Increased hysteresis from 3->6 windows and added a 30s cooldown; added tests for cooldown behavior.
Priya Shah: microbench numbers look strong but add a smaller end-to-end chat test with real prompts to ensure quality of generated tokens is unchanged.
Author: Added an e2e quality smoke check using standard prompts and BLEU/ROUGE-like heuristics; no regression observed.
release_notes: Add runtime opt-in: attention contracts and KV slot scaling to improve MQA/GQA model throughput and reduce KV memory amplification. Opt-in behind feature flags: enable_attn_contracts, enable_kv_slot_scaler. Expected p95 latency improvements 12-16% and KV memory reduction ~22% on mixed-prefix workloads.
notes: Canary plan attached in docs/perf/attn_contracts.md. No breaking API changes; transport header extension is backwards compatible.
